stem.text: Let \( f(x) = 3\left(\sqrt[3]{x + 4}\right)^{5} - 5 \). Determine whether f is differentiable at \( x = -4 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is differentiable at \( x = -4 \) with \( f'(-4) = 0 \), because the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides.

worked_solution.text: f is continuous at \( x = -4 \), since \( f(-4) = -5 \) and the root is continuous everywhere.
The difference quotient is \( \frac{f(-4 + h) - f(-4)}{h} = 3h^{\frac{2}{3}} \), and the exponent \( \frac{2}{3} \) is positive.
So the difference quotient approaches 0 from both sides, f is differentiable at \( x = -4 \), and \( f'(-4) = 0 \). The tangent line there is horizontal.

options.label: f is not differentiable at \( x = -4 \), because a sketch of the graph of f shows a sharp point at \( x = -4 \), where the root is 0.
options.derivation: non-differentiability read off the look of a sketch near the root, with no difference quotient examined

options.label: f is not differentiable at \( x = -4 \), because \( f'(x) = 5\left(\sqrt[3]{x + 4}\right)^{2} \) is 0 there, so the tangent is vertical.
options.derivation: a zero derivative read as a vertical tangent instead of a horizontal one

options.label: f is differentiable at \( x = -4 \), because f is continuous at \( x = -4 \), and every continuous function is differentiable.
options.derivation: differentiability concluded from continuity, the implication run backwards, with no slope computed
